title: Minimizing Labeling, Maximizing Performance: A Novel Approach to Nanoscale Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) Defect Segmentation
problem: Defect segmentation in semiconductor manufacturing requires large, labor-intensive labeled datasets and existing deep learning methods focus on macroscopic wafer defects rather than nanoscale morphology. Accurately segmenting nanoscale SEM defects is critical but challenging due to data scarcity.
motivation: Pinpointing nanoscale wafer defects is crucial for semiconductor yield and reliability.
method: The system uses a two-stage process: first locating and cropping to a defective region, then precisely outlining its exact boundaries. Weak supervision—learning from partially labeled images instead of fully annotated ones—cuts the labeling work needed while keeping accuracy equal to fully supervised methods. Testing on 1,328 real SEM images from a semiconductor manufacturing facility confirmed this approach.
key_novelty: A two-stage approach using weak supervision (learning from images with partial labels) achieves the same accuracy as fully labeled approaches while requiring only 10% of the labeling effort for nanoscale SEM defects.
contributions: Hybrid two-stage network architecture combining defect localization and detailed segmentation
Weakly supervised approach reducing labeling effort to 10% while maintaining fully supervised performance
Real-world validation on 1,328 facility SEM images demonstrating practical effectiveness
Outperforms existing weakly supervised methods while matching fully supervised baselines

metrics.labeling_efficiency: 10% of fully supervised labeling effort required

primary_theme: Weak supervision for semiconductor defect detection
